quote: Send me an email or send a hard copy
stewart_read: This is squarely the send_proposal_before_meeting trigger; the canonical response is to hold the no-email-proposals line while explaining why. Rep instead pushed to continue the phone Q&A without acknowledging her request.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the request as a stall he could out-persist rather than a hard objection requiring the script's 'we don't email proposals, our consultant explains it' line — but that reading isn't supported since he never delivered any version of that line.
coaching_implication: Should have run: 'Our policy is we don't send proposals over email because they need full explanation — that's why we set a quick call with a specialist.' Instead he repeated 'three more questions.'

quote: Okay. Well, we don't so everything we do is specific to homes. So we would just have to ask a couple questions
stewart_read: Second touch on the same request; rep gives a vague scope justification instead of the hard-rule script or any reframe, and doesn't acknowledge her stated frustration.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be an improvised attempt at redirect_to_design strategy, but it lacks the actual redirect (no mention of a specialist call or design) — it's just a soft stall.
coaching_implication: Coach the canonical line verbatim or in the rep's own words, but it must include WHY (proposals need explanation) and WHAT'S NEXT (a specific short call), not just 'we need info.'

quote: I'm not required to answer your questions on the phone.
stewart_read: Third and final touch; rep concedes immediately and ends the call, the critical_failure grade per the schema's deviation_grades for this rebuttal.
alternative_hypothesis: One could argue conceding was correct de-escalation given she was clearly closing the door — but the concession came with zero attempt at an alternative (offer callback, confirm mailing address for a proposal per her request), so it's a full drop, not a graceful exit.
coaching_implication: Even in concession, rep should have confirmed a concrete next step: 'I'll have this mailed to your address on file' — turning her own request into a controlled next touch instead of a dead end.

quote: Oh, so you haven't gotten enough information about me to to get to send you a quote?
stewart_read: She reveals she already has two competing quotes, which per the schema is a comparison_framing opportunity (already_saw_design rebuttal) — rep never engages this at all.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have been too focused on de-escalating the email request to catch this secondary disclosure — plausible given the call's rapid decline, but it's still a missed data point about her competitive context.
coaching_implication: Should acknowledge: 'Good, then this gives you a third comparison point' — cheap, low-effort validation that could have re-opened the door.

quote: Is there anybody else? And then the title is in your name.
stewart_read: Rep asks the co-owner question but immediately answers it himself/moves past it ('the title is in your name') without waiting for or capturing her actual response, per verified events marking this item only 'partial.'
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have been reading off a checklist and assumed single-owner status from the form, but that assumption bypasses required verification per verify.title_co_owners.
coaching_implication: Ask co-owner as a standalone question and wait for the answer — critical for spouse/co-decider inclusion later.

quote: electric bill. Yeah. I can help you right now.
stewart_read: Rep talks over the customer while she's mid-sentence stating her request, a procedural misstep that compounds the objection-handling failure — she has to say 'Are you there?' to regain the floor.
coaching_implication: Let the customer finish the sentence before responding; interrupting mid-request reads as not listening, which is exactly what she's complaining about.
